page: Microsoft Azure E64-32s_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine engineered with a high memory-to-vCPU ratio. Built on Microsoft Hyper-V, the instance runs on an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8370C processor clocked at 2.8 GHz. It is provisioned with 16 physical cores and 32 dedicated vCPUs with hyperthreading active, backed by 48 KB L1 data cache, 1 MB L2 cache, and 48 MB of L3 cache. Memory capacity stands at 512.0 GB, providing 16.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The instance does not include a GPU or bundled local storage, operating as a diskless compute node that relies on network-attached Premium Storage.

Benchmark results highlight strong memory subsystem performance, scoring in the top 25% for PassMark memory alongside uncached large-block read throughput of 205.66 GB/sec and write throughput of 116.03 GB/sec. General compute metrics align within the middle 50% average tier, yielding a PassMark CPU score of 37,169.96, a Geekbench multi-core score of 13,936.0, and 31,074.98 points in multi-core stress-ng tests. In-memory data structures perform solidly, evidenced by Redis achieving 31.69 million SET operations per second and database operation scores of 15,446.45.

Hardware tradeoffs center on the constraint of CPU-only execution without local ephemeral storage. While instruction set extensions like AVX-512 and VNNI assist basic inference—delivering 253.47 tokens per second on 135M parameter models—the absence of dedicated accelerators causes large 70B parameter prompt processing to drop to 6.45 tokens per second. Resource efficiency is maximized in workflows where large active working sets require memory density rather than intensive CPU core scaling.

The Azure E64-32s_v5 is well suited for memory-intensive enterprise workloads, including large in-memory caching layers, relational database servers, enterprise resource planning applications, and ETL pipelines that process massive datasets entirely within system memory.
